label: STOPP C9
title: Anticoagulant for a first lung clot beyond 12 months
statement: Vitamin K antagonist, direct thrombin inhibitor or factor Xa inhibitors for first pulmonary embolus without continuing provoking risk factors (e.g., thrombophilia) for longer than 12 months (no proven added benefit).

source.document: O'Mahony D, et al. STOPP/START criteria for potentially inappropriate prescribing in older people: version 3. Eur Geriatr Med 2023;14:625-632, Appendix 1 (corrected supplementary file; NHS Somerset copy used for text, sentence-identical to the earlier parse)
source.citation: O'Mahony D, Cherubini A, Guiteras AR, et al. STOPP/START criteria for potentially inappropriate prescribing in older people: version 3. Eur Geriatr Med 2023;14:625-632. doi:10.1007/s41999-023-00777-y
source.credit: O'Mahony D, Cherubini A, Guiteras AR, et al. STOPP/START criteria for potentially inappropriate prescribing in older people: version 3. Eur Geriatr Med 2023;14:625-632. doi:10.1007/s41999-023-00777-y

plain_summary: A blood thinner taken for longer than 12 months after a first pulmonary embolism (a clot in the lung) with no continuing cause has no proven extra benefit and adds bleeding risk. Australian guidance differs: the Thrombosis and Haemostasis Society of Australia and New Zealand (2019) supports extended anticoagulation after a first unprovoked pulmonary embolism when the bleeding risk is low, at full or reduced dose. This flag asks why treatment continues, not for stopping.

medicine_groups.name: Anticoagulants used in this rule
medicine_groups.note: Warfarin is the vitamin K antagonist. Dabigatran is the direct thrombin inhibitor. Apixaban, rivaroxaban, edoxaban and fondaparinux are factor Xa inhibitors. No Australian brand is listed for edoxaban. Fondaparinux is an injection. Heparin and enoxaparin are not in this group. Aspirin and clopidogrel are not anticoagulants. Generic packs that show the ingredient name with a company name count too.

needs_facts.what: Link between this anticoagulant course and the first pulmonary embolism
needs_facts.meets: A first pulmonary embolism is documented. Identify the start of anticoagulation for that clot or the first supply linked to it.

options.words: This course treated the first pulmonary embolism
This course treated a recurrent embolism or was solely for another reason

needs_facts.what: Continuing provoking risk or other ongoing indication
needs_facts.meets: Follow-up documents no continuing provoking risk factor or separate ongoing indication. The first embolism may have been unprovoked or followed a temporary factor that has resolved.

options.words: No provoking risk factor continues and there is no other indication for extended anticoagulation
A provoking risk factor continues or there is another indication for extended anticoagulation

needs_facts.what: Duration of anticoagulation for the first pulmonary embolism
needs_facts.meets: Use dated anticoagulation clinic or treatment records to establish whether one course for this embolism lasted longer than twelve calendar months.

options.words: One course continued beyond twelve calendar months
No single course continued beyond twelve calendar months

rule_for_models: Apply from age 65. Confirm an unknown age before reporting a finding. Look for a first pulmonary embolism, no continuing provoking risk factor and no separate ongoing indication for anticoagulation. Include an unprovoked first embolism and a first embolism after a resolved temporary factor, whether major or minor. Check that a single Group A course for this clot extended beyond 12 calendar months. Use the documented treatment start or first supply linked to that clot. Use supply dates, quantities and directions to work out cover when a daily dose is known. For variable-dose warfarin, use dated treatment or INR dosing notes confirming continuous therapy for the same clot beyond 12 months. Linked repeat supplies spanning that interval support a possible finding if continuity is uncertain. Never infer a daily tablet count from directions to follow the INR. For any Group A medicine with unclear directions, do not infer a daily dose from the pack size. Do not join separate courses. If the supply pattern could qualify but dose records or gaps leave duration uncertain, report a possible finding and name "Duration of anticoagulation for the first pulmonary embolism" as missing only when the other evidence could qualify. Check dated clinic or treatment records for the dose taken and any breaks. A confirmed course longer than twelve calendar months establishes duration only. Cite the supporting record. If no single course exceeded twelve calendar months there is no finding. If continuity is still uncertain or duration is recorded as Not known, the finding remains possible when the other evidence could qualify. Exclude recurrent embolism, continuing provoking risk, a separate ongoing indication or treatment of 12 months or less. Cite the first embolism, evidence about ongoing risk and indication, and the linked treatment dates. If the pattern could qualify but these facts are unclear, report a possible finding and name the missing evidence. Request review of the documented plan. Extended anticoagulation after an unprovoked embolism can be appropriate in Australia.
cannot_be_seen: Whether the clot was a first one, what caused it, whether a clotting disorder or cancer is present, and whether the blood thinner is also needed for another reason such as an irregular heartbeat (atrial fibrillation). Also medicines supplied by a hospital or another pharmacy.
ask_the_gp: Whether the blood thinner is still needed, given the cause of the clot and the time already taken, and whether a review of the planned length of treatment is due.
